- tests/fixtures/validation_harness/repo_local_tooling/tests/20_import_audit.sh:22 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3-coder-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Redirecting both streams to `/dev/null` suppresses the import audit helper's failure diagnostics.
  WHY: When an import fails, `import_audit.py` writes module-specific failure details to stderr, but the script discards that stream and only reports `# import audit failed`, so CI failures lack specifics.
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/repo-local-tooling/tests/20_import_audit.sh.j2:22 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v3_2, minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The template uses the same redirection, so the import audit helper's failure diagnostics are suppressed there too.
  WHY: The generated script behaves the same way, so the details written to stderr on import failure are lost and consumer-repo CI failures are harder to debug.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===
- tests/fixtures/validation_harness/repo_local_tooling/tests/20_import_audit.sh:22 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Redirecting stderr to `/dev/null` suppresses valuable diagnostic information when import audit fails.
  WHY: When a Python module fails to import, the `import_audit.py` helper prints error details (which module failed and traceback) to stderr, but `2>&1` sends that diagnostics stream to `/dev/null`, so CI failures lack specifics.
- workflow-templates/validation-harness/repo-local-tooling/tests/20_import_audit.sh.j2:22 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Same issue - redirecting stderr suppresses diagnostics in template.
  WHY: Template generates the same problematic code, propagating the issue to consumer repos using this validation harness family.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v3_2 ===

- tests/fixtures/validation_harness/repo_local_tooling/tests/20_import_audit.sh:22 (and equivalent in workflow-templates file) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The change from `python3 ... >/dev/null` to `python3 ... >/dev/null 2>&1` suppresses the specific module failure details and error diagnostics emitted to stderr.
  WHY: When the import audit fails, the script now only emits the generic `# import audit failed` message, so CI failures are harder to debug.
